newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline rises on refiner buying.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline rises on refiner buying.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline prices firmed in Chicago late Tuesday on sightings of a major regional refiner seeking prompt barrels, traders said.
Traders said BP was still in the market for spot product as it struggled to return a catalytic cracker at its 161,000 barrel per day Lima, Ohio refinery to service.
"There's been a lack of refiner selling, and BP is buying because of the cat cracker," one trader said.
Aside from firmer unleaded differentials in Chicago, products prices in the Midwest markets were largely tracking the Merc as trade wound down Tuesday.
Chicago unleaded for early September deliveries firmed to bids 0.25 cent under NYMEX October unleaded with later deliveries 0.50 cents under the print. Premium was talked 3.25 cents higher.
Group Three unleaded gasoline was discussed 1.25/1.50 cents a gallon over the print for late-August deliveries, with premium 3.75 cents higher.
Chicago low sulphur diesel for September deliveries was unchanged at 1.75/2.0 cents over the NYMEX October heating oil.
Group Three low sulphur diesel remained 3.25/3.50 cents a gallon over the print for late-August deliveries, traders said.
High sulphur diesel was bid 0.75 cent over the print for September deliveries in Chicago and 1.25 cents over the print for late-August deliveries in Group Three, traders said.
